correctness.rationale: PASS: In each power-of-two cyclic direction, multiplication by x+x^{-1}=x^{-1}(x+1)^2 has rank n-2j in power j and consists of two nilpotent blocks of size n/2. The tensor module is 2^d copies of a rectangular truncated polynomial ring. Replacing a largest-side generator t_k by w=sum_i t_i, the Frobenius identity at H=max_i(n_i/2) gives t_k^H=w^H; this is an invertible coordinate substitution, so spatial adjacency has N/H blocks J_H(0). For F=[[A,I],[I,0]], the identity F^2+I=diag(A,A)F gives (F+I)^{2H}=0, while ker(F+I) has dimension ker(A)=N/H. Dimension and block-length bounds force exactly N/H Jordan blocks J_{2H}(1). Fixed counts and exact least-period differences then follow. Exact independent physical-grid and polynomial-basis verifiers replayed on d=3 and d=4 cases; their finite scope is not conflated with proof of all d.

originality.rationale: PASS, qualified: Claim is restricted to the new d>=3 power-of-two periodic-boundary, two-time-level wave similarity and complete orbit census. Martin-Odlyzko-Wolfram (1984) explicitly develop group algebra for multidimensional first-order rules and discuss higher-order linear rules, but Theorem 4.8 assumes side lengths indivisible by the characteristic, and Section 4E does not derive the present combined multidimensional wave rank/Jordan formula. Macfarlane (2004) restricts to one-dimensional reversible waves. Chang et al. (2017) analyze one-time-level multidimensional Kronecker sums principally with null boundary, and general Jordan algorithms do not state the claimed periodic-boundary two-layer exact uniform blocks. Previously available one-dimensional waves and two-dimensional first-order torus results are excluded from originality, not counted as fresh discoveries. Targeted published-record searches yielded no stronger covering formula; an unindexed equivalent algebraic derivation remains possible.

value.rationale: PASS: This natural nearest-neighbor reversible wave on every characteristic-two power-of-two hypertorus of dimension >=3 has an unexpected uniform unipotent representation. Global period depends only on the longest circumference, not dimension or the other side lengths, while the complete orbit populations depend exactly on transverse volume. The proof uses an essential multivariate Frobenius coordinate transformation and yields complete infinite-family fixed-point and primitive-cycle information, not a single numerical example or a restatement of reversibility.
